messages:
ACME Ops: hitting a big spike of 502/504s on hosted API since ~08:12 UTC, impacting streaming requests. customer report: "many of our /v1/generate streams just cut with 502, some 504s. no change on our side, started after ~08:10"
ACME Ops: example trace-id: trace-0a1b2c3d; request-id: r-9f8e7d6c; region: us-west-2. attaching a quick repro curl we run:```bash
for i in {1..50}; do
  curl -s -D - -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","input":"long prompt...", "stream":true}' &
done; wait
```
Marie (Support): sorry about that — escalating. can you confirm customer org id and whether this is only streaming endpoints or also non-streaming? :eyes:
ACME Ops: org acme-42, mostly streaming, but some non-streaming 502s too. happens under bursty parallel traffic (we push lots of small client requests concurrently).
Jake (prodmon-bot): alert: edge-502-rate spike at 08:12 UTC (+380% vs baseline). top error: upstream_reset / connection_reset_by_peer. affected zone: us-west-2-edge. linked alert: https://monitoring.redwood/internal/alerts/ALRT-2330
Omar (Eng-SRE): thanks — initial hypothesis: upstream (auth/billing) or connection pool exhaustion at edge->auth path. can you grab the full request headers for one failing request (particularly x-request-id, x-trace, x-forwarded-for)? also sending envoy access log sample helps.
ACME Ops: pasted one access log line: ```2026-03-16T08:12:15Z envoy us-west-2 edgeproxy r-9f8e7d6c POST /v1/generate 502 "upstream reset" "connection reset by peer" rt=1203ms ua="acme-client/2.3"```
Tia (Edge): seeing matching spikes on edge nodes. env logs show a lot of HTTP/2 RST_STREAM and GOAWAY in the same window. sample from envoy stderr: ```[warning] [upstream] upstream remote close: reset reason: connection termination, stream 0, err=ENOTCONN, code=2```
Tia (Edge): probable root cause: h2 stream saturation between edge and auth/billing microservice — when the pool hits max concurrent streams, Envoy closes connections -> upstream resets -> 502s for downstream streaming requests. streaming keeps connections open longer which exacerbates.
Omar (Eng-SRE): agree. quick repro steps we ran in staging: run the curl-parallel loop with stream:true and a small auth delay stub, we see connection pool drain fast and resets. command to inspect pool stats: ```kubectl exec -c envoy -it $(kubectl get pod -l app=edge -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- curl -s localhost:9901/stats | grep upstream_cx_http2``` (shows many cx_destroy).
Marie (Support): immediate mitigation suggestions? customer is getting urgent calls.
Omar (Eng-SRE): short-term: 1) throttle concurrent streaming requests per org (rate-limit tokens) 2) increase upstream http2_max_concurrent_streams config on Envoy for auth service (bump from 100 to 300) and increase connection pool size, 3) enable 502->retry with jitter on client side (3 retries) for idempotent calls. 4) restart a few auth pods to clear stuck connections if needed. Any one of these reduces pressure quickly.
Tia (Edge): adding config snippet we applied in staging to increase streams: ```network_filters:
  - name: envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager
    typed_config:
      '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.http_connection_manager.v3.HttpConnectionManager
      upstream_http_protocol_options:
        common_http_protocol_options:
          max_concurrent_streams: 300```
Tia (Edge): note this is conservative, upstream service must also accept increased MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS. coordinated deploy needed.
ACME Ops: we tried throttling client concurrency on our side to ~10 parallel, errors dropped to near-zero within 3 minutes. can you apply a short-term rate-limit?
Marie (Support): have queued an emergency config change with Edge infra to add org-level concurrency cap for acme-42 and a global soft cap for streaming endpoints. change id: CHG-8421. ETA 12m.
Jake (prodmon-bot): change CHG-8421 applied to 3/edge nodes at 08:24 UTC.
Omar (Eng-SRE): follow-up: we should also instrument auth's HTTP/2 settings and connection metrics, add upstream circuit-breaker on auth path to fail fast, and add a model-routing fallback so streaming traffic can hit a lower-latency model when auth is slow. I'll open a postmortem PR with recommended config diffs.
ACME Ops: thanks — after throttling + small pod restart we see errors go away. please keep us posted; we'll hold the client-side throttle for 24h while you make edge changes. :thumbsup:
Marie (Support): marking P0->P1, will close thread after postmortem. tagging @Omar @Tia for postmortem notes and remediation actions.
Omar (Eng-SRE): noted — will include repro, config patch, and monitoring dashboards (upstream_cx, h2_streams, auth_latency) in the postmortem.
ACME Ops: appreciated — please cc when postmortem ready.
